articles.author: David M. Jackson
articles.headline: Netflix's Post-Earnings Selloff: Trapped By Its Own Success
articles.summary:
Netflix just delivered the kind of quarter most CEOs would frame on their wall. Revenue up. Margins healthy. Strategy firing on all cylinders. Etc. 



And the market’s response? A selloff.



To the casual observer, it
articles._summary: Netflix just delivered the kind of quarter most CEOs would frame on their wall. Revenue up. Margins healthy. Strategy firing on all cylinders. Etc. To the casual observer, it looks like insanity. But seasoned players understand something darker at work here: a brutal logic that governs not just stocks, but power itself: The crowd doesn’t judge you by your performance. It judges you by the story it already told itself about you. Netflix didn’t stumble. It simply failed to outrun its own legend. Netflix the business is objectively stronger today than it was three months ago. Both statements are true. The disconnect exists because you’re not buying a company when you click “buy”. Instead, you’re buying a future that may or may not arrive. And that future was already priced for perfection. When a company makes excellence look routine, the market stops rewarding it for excellence. It starts demanding miracles.
articles._zh_headline: Netflix 的财报后抛售：受困于自身的成功
articles._zh_summary: Netflix刚刚发布了大多数首席执行官都会在墙上画框的季度业绩。收入上去了。利润率健康。战略全速运转。对于不经意的观察者来说，这看起来像是精神错乱。但经验丰富的玩家明白这里有一些更黑暗的东西：一种残酷的逻辑，不仅控制着股票，还控制着权力本身：人群不会根据你的表现来评判你。它根据它已经讲述的关于你的故事来评判你。 Netflix 并没有陷入困境。它只是未能超越自己的传奇。 Netflix 今天的业务客观上比三个月前更强劲。两种说法都是正确的。这种脱节的存在是因为当你点击“购买”时，你并不是在购买一家公司。相反，你购买的是一个可能到来也可能不会到来的未来。而这个未来已经为完美定价。当一家公司让卓越看起来司空见惯时，市场就会不再奖励它的卓越表现。它开始要求奇迹。

articles.headline: US Debt Surpasses 100% of GDP for the First Time Since World War II— Is the Fiscal Squeeze Actually Deflationary?
articles.summary: U.S. debt surpasses 100% of GDP for the first time since WWII. Discover why experts argue this $39.4T fiscal squeeze might be deflationary.
articles._summary: Publicly held federal debt has officially eclipsed the size of the entire American economy , crossing the 100% gross domestic product (GDP) threshold for the first time since 1946. While traditional economic theory warns that this fiscal squeeze could trigger runaway inflation, a growing chorus of contrarian analysts argues that the massive debt load might actually be deflationary. Instead, experts point to decades of chronic legislative inaction.
articles._zh_headline: 美国债务二战以来首次超过GDP的100%——财政紧缩真的是通货紧缩吗？

articles.headline: Former Fed Economist Claudia Sahm Says Kevin Warsh Is 'Unanchored From Inflation Data'
articles.summary: Former Fed economist Claudia Sahm criticized Chair Kevin Warsh, saying the Fed's definition of price stability has become unclear.
articles._summary: Former Federal Reserve economist Claudia Sahm on Friday criticized Fed Chair Kevin Warsh ‘s recent comments on inflation, saying the central bank’s definition of price stability has become unclear under his leadership. In a blog titled “2% of What?”, Sahm said the Fed’s commitment to price stability loses meaning if policymakers do not use a common measure to define it. She added that Warsh has repeatedly referred to restoring price stability while stopping short of explicitly identifying the benchmark used to measure it. Since taking office, Warsh has reaffirmed the Fed’s 2% inflation target but has not publicly referenced the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index during his confirmation hearing, first press conference, congressional testimony, or other public appearances, according to Sahm. “The Fed worries about unanchored inflation expectations; I am starting to worry about a Fed Chair who is unanchored from inflation data,” Sahm said in a post on X.

articles._summary: Micron is one of the largest semiconductor companies in the world, specializing in memory and storage chips. Its primary revenue stream comes from dynamic random access memory, or DRAM, and it also has minority exposure to not-and or NAND, flash chips. Micron serves a global customer base, selling chips into data centers, mobile phones, consumer electronics, and industrial and automotive applications. The firm is vertically integrated.

articles.author: Radhika Anilkumar Nadig
articles.headline: Ross Gerber Slams 'Bubble Talk' as Earnings Season Begins: 'AI Is No Fad' and 'Valuations Are Quite Nice'
articles.summary: Ross Gerber urged investors to look past the tech selloff, dismissing AI bubble fears and calling the sector a long-term opportunity.
articles._summary: Ross Gerber of investment firm Gerber Kawasaki told investors to look past the recent technology selloff on Thursday, dismissing fears of an AI bubble, saying the sector remained a long-term opportunity. In a post on X, Gerber said stocks were in “sell mode” just as earnings season got underway, with investors raising doubts about valuations after the recent pullback. Gerber dismissed concerns that the weakness reflected an AI bubble, saying there was “no bubble talk” despite growing skepticism around the sector.
articles._zh_headline: 财报季开始之际，罗斯·格伯 (Ross Gerber) 猛烈抨击“泡沫言论”：“人工智能并非时尚”且“估值相当不错”
articles._zh_summary: 周四，投资公司格柏川崎 (Gerber Kawasaki) 的罗斯·格柏 (Ross Gerber) 告诉投资者，不要忽视最近的科技股抛售，他消除了对人工智能泡沫的担忧，称该行业仍然是一个长期机会。格伯在 X 上发表的一篇文章中表示，就在财报季节开始之际，股票正处于“卖出模式”，投资者在最近的回调后对估值提出了怀疑。格伯驳斥了有关疲软反映人工智能泡沫的担忧，称尽管对该行业的怀疑与日俱增，但“没有泡沫言论”。
